rows.sourceExcerpt: They are conditional tools whose legitimacy depends on design and on their accountable connection to the decisions they are meant to inform.
rows.rationale: La pregunta pide «Which statement best expresses the writer’s conclusion?» y la clave es «Citizens’ juries can add value when their design and link to authority are accountable.». La evidencia dice «They are conditional tools whose legitimacy depends on design and on their accountable connection to the decisions they are meant to inform.». La coincidencia semántica se apoya en «design», «accountable»: esos elementos enlazan el foco de la pregunta y la opción con la información del pasaje, mientras las demás opciones carecen de ese vínculo en el tramo citado.
rows.sourceLedgerRationale: Option A accurately paraphrases the conditional conclusion.

responseBinding.questionText: Container: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: For a booked test, the container we supply is a sterile bottle, not a household jar. You can collect it here without charge before sampling.

responseBinding.questionText: Address: Flat 6, ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: That is helpful. Could we make the booking now? My address is Flat Six, Celyn Court. That is Celyn, C E L Y N, on Penarth Road.

responseBinding.questionText: Sample outlet: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: The bathroom sometimes tastes metallic, but it is rarely used. I will take the official sample from the kitchen tap because we use that cold-water outlet every day.

responseBinding.questionText: Collection time: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: I leave for work just before seven. I can collect it at six forty-five, then bring it straight to you. Please record 6:45, not seven.

responseBinding.questionText: During transport: keep the bottle ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Keep the sealed bottle cool during the journey, but do not freeze it. A small insulated bag is fine; loose ice must not touch the cap.

responseBinding.questionText: Report delivery: results ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Yes. Select results portal on the form. We will email when the report is ready.

responseBinding.questionText: Why does Anwen decide not to collect the sample on Sunday?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: The sample would have to be stored too long.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Correct. We are closed on Sunday, and holding the bottle until Monday would make the recorded conditions less useful. Wednesday morning is available.

responseBinding.questionText: Why should Anwen run the tap before filling the bottle?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: To sample supplied water after flushing.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Not for the package you are choosing. Run the cold tap for two minutes first. The test is intended to describe the supplied water after flushing, not water that stood overnight.

responseBinding.questionText: Which testing package does Anwen choose?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The flat has old internal pipes, so the metals panel sounds most relevant. I considered the full package, but nobody has been ill and I do not need that broader service.

responseBinding.questionText: What does Caspian say about the faster service?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The standard metals panel is eighty-two pounds. Results take five working days. A faster two-day service exists, but it costs substantially more.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the conifer walk?

bindings.audiblePhrase: For the conifer walk, follow the winter loop north from the main gate and keep left at the first fork. Pass the lower western bend and continue to the upper bend immediately south of the triangular Young Eucalypts plot.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the warming shelter?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Visitors who need a warm break should return to the fork and take the short eastern spur. The warming shelter is the square building immediately south of Lookout Road.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the accessible viewing deck?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The accessible viewing deck is farther east. Pass the rectangular bed beside the central lawn, then take the map’s only short blue dead-end spur towards North Creek. The broad platform at the spur’s end is the deck.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the storm-damaged bridge?

bindings.audiblePhrase: A storm damaged the timber bridge north of the creek. It appears on the map between the platform and the research plots, but barriers close both approaches today.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the glasshouse?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The glasshouse is the oval building at the western end of Lookout Road, just north of the conifer curve. Its public entrance faces east, towards the road.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the shuttle bus bay?

bindings.audiblePhrase: At the end of your visit, the shuttle bus will collect passengers from the bay directly east of the main gate. The ordinary public bus stop is outside the map.

responseBinding.questionText: Which feature is highlighted in the Alpine sector?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Now I will suggest what to notice in four sectors. In the Alpine sector, low conifers form sheltered shapes that remain easy to examine even when the exposed beds are frosty.

responseBinding.questionText: Which feature is highlighted in the Eucalypt sector?

bindings.audiblePhrase: In the Eucalypt sector, winter light makes differences in bark colour particularly clear. Flowers are scarce there in July, despite what an old leaflet suggests.

responseBinding.questionText: Which feature is highlighted in the Rainforest sector?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: an indoor display about leaf structure

bindings.audiblePhrase: The Rainforest sector has an indoor interpretation display beside the humid house. Its labels explain leaf structure; the outdoor sound installation is switched off this season.

responseBinding.questionText: Which feature is highlighted in the Research plots?

bindings.audiblePhrase: At the Research plots, staff have left numbered tags beside the winter measurements. You may read them from the path, but they are working labels rather than a public exhibition.

responseBinding.questionText: What do the students identify as the most serious flaw in the pilot study?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: The meters recorded at different times.

bindings.audiblePhrase: That is the most serious flaw in the pilot because we compared readings as if they were simultaneous. We should synchronise both clocks before every session.

responseBinding.questionText: What was wrong with the original occupancy record?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: It did not track changes during measurement.

bindings.audiblePhrase: And several students arrived while we were taking readings. I suggest a simple door count at each measurement, then a brief occupancy log with arrival changes.

responseBinding.questionText: What do they decide to do about blind positions?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: record them with photographs and codes

bindings.audiblePhrase: A photograph from the doorway plus a simple position code would make that condition repeatable. We should never adjust a blind without recording it.

responseBinding.questionText: Which rooms will form the main comparison?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: two similar rooms with different shading

bindings.audiblePhrase: That creates too many confounds. Two rooms of similar size and orientation, but with different shading devices, would give a cleaner comparison.

responseBinding.questionText: Which sampling schedule do they choose?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: fixed paired times with repeats if needed

bindings.audiblePhrase: Let us take paired readings at fixed morning, midday and afternoon times, with a documented contingency if cloud changes sharply during a pair.

responseBinding.questionText: Which revision addresses this problem: the meters give different values?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: check both instruments against a reference

bindings.audiblePhrase: I would check both instruments against the same reference before taking any classroom readings. That should show whether one meter needs recalibration.

responseBinding.questionText: Which revision addresses this problem: tables have been moved?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: mark the tripod positions on the floor

bindings.audiblePhrase: For tables that have moved, removable floor markers will restore the tripod positions. The floor plan remains useful, but it was not enough by itself.

responseBinding.questionText: Which revision addresses this problem: occupancy changes during a reading?

bindings.audiblePhrase: When occupancy changes during a reading, we will count users at that measurement and note arrivals. We need totals, never names.

responseBinding.questionText: Which revision addresses this problem: blind positions are inconsistent?

bindings.audiblePhrase: For inconsistent blind positions, we will photograph the setting and assign it a simple code. That is clearer than writing adjusted.

responseBinding.questionText: Which revision addresses this problem: cloud cover changes rapidly?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Finally, if cloud cover changes rapidly, we will repeat the paired readings. We can trial the revised sheet tomorrow before the three-day study begins.

responseBinding.questionText: Spring inflow may deposit pale ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: A common pair forms because seasonal processes deliver different material. During spring snowmelt, streams may carry pale silt into the basin in a relatively energetic pulse.

responseBinding.questionText: A darker summer layer may contain ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Later, calmer summer conditions can allow darker organic material to settle. Together, the contrasting light and dark layers may represent one year.

responseBinding.questionText: A ______ can preserve delicate surface layers.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Where the recent surface is essential, researchers may use a freeze corer. Frozen sediment adheres to the sampling face and can preserve delicate upper layers more clearly.

responseBinding.questionText: Fine layer pairs may be counted using a ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Back in the laboratory, the core is split, photographed and described. Investigators may count layer pairs under a microscope where boundaries are too fine for the unaided eye. High-resolution images let analysts revisit the same boundary and document why a doubtful line was included or rejected.

responseBinding.questionText: One possible marker horizon is ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: A marker horizon provides an external checkpoint. A distinctive volcanic ash layer, for example, may be linked to a dated eruption if its identity is independently established.

responseBinding.questionText: Mixing by organisms is called ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: One major disturbance is bioturbation, the mixing of sediment by organisms. Burrowing can blur boundaries, redistribute particles and make an apparently smooth band span more than one season.

responseBinding.questionText: Which independent method can check a varve chronology?

bindings.audiblePhrase: At this stage, the chronology itself needs a test independent of visual counting. Radiometric dating can check an interval against physical decay, so agreement supports the count without simply repeating the analyst’s judgement.

responseBinding.questionText: What type of retrieval damage can shorten the recovered sequence?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Core compression is particularly important because it shortens the recovered sequence and changes apparent layer thickness. Smearing mainly obscures boundaries, while a gap removes material altogether; none should be treated as an ordinary annual transition.

responseBinding.questionText: What should researchers compare to separate local and regional patterns?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The stronger spatial test is comparison across multiple lakes. If separately dated records show the same transition, a broader process becomes more plausible, although agreement alone does not explain the mechanism.

responseBinding.questionText: What can varves alone not identify?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Most importantly, varves establish timing and association more readily than exact causes. A causal claim needs independent environmental evidence, a plausible mechanism and an account of alternatives that the observations do not rule out.
